Bitcoin just had its worst stretch in years — and it's no longer only a crypto story.

It fell to about $55,000 on Saturday, its lowest in two years, before rebounding toward $60,000. That's down more than 20% this month and over 50% below the $126,000 record it hit on Oct. 6, 2025 (Crypto Briefing, Nov. 20-21).

Why it matters even if you never bought any: spot bitcoin now sits in brokerage accounts, some 401(k)s and Canadian crypto ETFs. The same AI-valuation fear that pulled the Nasdaq negative for 2026 is now spilling into crypto. The Fear & Greed Index reads 11 — 'extreme fear.'

My take: weekends like this run on leverage and forced selling, not on people changing their minds about bitcoin.

Does a 50% drop make bitcoin look risky to you, or cheap?
